channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: Justice Department probes networks over White House pool boycott
item.description: The Justice Department opened an antitrust inquiry into ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News after the networks collectively stopped White House pool coverage when reporters from CNN, Politico and MS NOW lost credentials. The case turns a press-access dispute into a test of whether coordinated newsroom action can be treated as a commercial group boycott.

item.title: The problem with Facebook was Facebook
item.description: John Herrman argues that years of reform debates mistook Facebook's harms for correctable lapses instead of consequences of its core attention-and-data business. Recommendation systems steadily displaced social connections with optimized, unfamiliar content, while changing corporate missions offered little accountability for the platform's underlying incentives.

item.title: Worker-owned Hell Gate tests a harder membership pitch
item.description: New York local outlet Hell Gate has about 11,000 paid subscriptions and has passed https://www.rssboard.org/rss-specification million in annual recurring revenue, but growth has slowed. The worker-owned newsroom is experimenting with occasional limits on free access, sharper membership appeals and events while keeping subscriber support central to its independence.

item.title: LoopConf trades corporate sponsors for attendee funding
item.description: Organizer Brian Richards explains why LoopConf US is relying on early ticket sales instead of corporate sponsorship. The 2027 WordPress developer conference will cap attendance at 100–200 people, use a lightweight static site and emphasize open-source resilience and cross-platform ideas.

item.title: Nieman Lab redesigns 100,000 pages without flattening them
item.description: Joshua Benton details Nieman Lab’s first major redesign in years: more art-directed story layouts, rebuilt archives, improved search and new beats for platforms, creators and local news. Migrating 12,000 articles and more than 100,000 URLs also required preserving a decade of custom CSS and hand-coded publishing history.

item.title: Open source moves to the center of Europe’s digital-sovereignty push
item.description: At Open Source Summit Europe, Linux Foundation leaders argued that Europe’s security and sovereignty policies converge on one practical need: trustworthy software supply chains. Open source can provide auditable, reusable infrastructure while reducing dependence on a few overseas cloud and platform vendors.

item.title: Rappler builds its own digital commons on an open protocol
item.description: Maria Ressa explains why Rappler stopped waiting for dominant platforms to protect journalism and built a community network using Matrix. The federated system links independent newsrooms, lets each govern itself and reaches readers without an engagement algorithm controlling distribution.

item.title: A practical path from Discord to a self-hosted Matrix server
item.description: Hackaday walks through replacing a closed chat platform with Matrix, an open standard whose servers and clients can be self-hosted, extended and bridged to other services. The account also confronts the hard part of decentralized software: choosing among tools and persuading a community to move.

item.title: TRACE project targets trustworthy attribution in scholarly publishing
item.description: Publishers, standards groups and libraries launched TRACE to coordinate content-exchange standards, provenance tracking and usage reporting for machine-assisted research. Its first projects address discovery and access, preserving attribution through the content lifecycle, and consistent measurement of content use.

item.title: Satellite-to-phone rules and a spectrum auction move forward
item.description: The FCC will vote Oct. 29 on advancing a spectrum auction and updating rules for phones that connect directly to satellites. The proposal would auction 25 megahertz and open another 482 megahertz for space-based coverage, as Starlink, Amazon and a carrier joint venture race to eliminate dead zones.

item.title: Global survey finds deepening doubt about social media and democracy
item.description: Pew found rising concern across 26 countries that social platforms divide people and damage democracy, even as majorities still say the services inform citizens and give them a political voice. In the United States, 64% of adults said social media harms democracy.

item.title: Press-freedom pressures rise across several countries
item.description: A weekly survey of press freedom tracks U.S. news organizations fighting White House access bans, the arrest of an independent Egyptian newsroom, threats that stopped a Brazilian outlet’s election coverage and Hong Kong’s first known journalist arrest for sedition under its 2024 security law. Bulgaria, meanwhile, adopted anti-SLAPP protections.

item.title: Microsoft and Nvidia move coding agents onto the PC
item.description: Microsoft and Nvidia are unveiling the Surface Laptop Ultra, built around RTX Spark chips that can run coding and business agents locally instead of in the cloud. The bet revives the PC as an independent computing platform, though soaring memory costs may push the machine beyond the reach of ordinary developers.

item.title: Independent media needs distribution, not just good reporting
item.description: Maya Tudor argues that journalism cannot defend democracy on reporting alone. Comparing Hungary, India, Poland and Sri Lanka, she finds independent outlets also need resilient distribution, networked alliances, diverse financing and legal defenses—especially when governments and platforms can dominate how citizens encounter news.

item.title: Open-source builders put interoperable agent protocols on the agenda
item.description: Google’s open-source roundup points developers toward an October summit session on how the vendor-neutral A2A and MCP protocols work together, alongside practical projects for local retrieval and transparent model inference. The common thread is familiar: useful scripting systems become more durable when their parts can interoperate.
